upstream_dwc2_history.message:
dwc2: keep class endpoint buffers when DMA may be selected at runtime

With both CFG_TUD_DWC2_DMA_ENABLE and CFG_TUD_DWC2_SLAVE_ENABLE set, the
driver picks Buffer DMA or Slave mode per controller at runtime (GHWCFG2),
but CFG_TUD_EDPT_DEDICATED_HWFIFO followed SLAVE_ENABLE alone. Classes then
dropped their endpoint buffers and used usbd_edpt_xfer_fifo(), which leaves
xfer->buffer NULL: on a DMA-capable core the endpoint DMA address became 0,
the core raised AHBERR and the endpoint NAKed forever (CDC write hang on
STM32H7S3 OTG_HS).

- CFG_TUD/TUH_EDPT_DEDICATED_HWFIFO = SLAVE && !DMA: a fifo transfer is only
  allowed when no runtime mode needs a linear buffer.
- CFG_TUSB_FIFO_HWFIFO_API follows SLAVE_ENABLE directly, so the slave path
  keeps its hwfifo helpers; tusb_fifo.h only defaults it.
- dcd_edpt_xfer_fifo() asserts when the controller runs Buffer DMA.

dcd/dwc2: keep GAHBCFG.GINT masked while SETUP DMA recovery is pending

osal_queue_receive() and spinlock operations re-enable the port interrupt,
undoing dcd_int_disable() before the deferred recovery runs. Clear the
core's global interrupt mask too; dcd_init() sets it again.

fix(dcd/dwc2): opt-in SETUP DMA guard for back-to-back short SETUP erratum

Work around the DWC2 Buffer-DMA erratum "Device Controller does not drop
short SETUP packets": more than three back-to-back SETUP packets, one of
them shorter than 5 bytes, can rewind DOEPDMA0 below the programmed
address and write SETUP data before the buffer.

Opt in with CFG_TUD_DWC2_DMA_SETUP_GUARD_SIZE (bytes, multiple of 8,
default 0 = disabled, no behavior change). When enabled, a guard is
reserved before the 3-packet SETUP area, Back2BackSETup is unmasked, and
a DOEPDMA0 inside the guard disconnects the device in the ISR and defers
a core re-init to task context. tud_dwc2_setup_dma_error_cb() is invoked
before the re-init.

The guard only covers the interrupt latency: guard ~= 12 + 4 * T_irq /
T_setup bytes; rough sizes are listed with the option.

Based on #4423 by Tomas Rezucha, rebased and reworked:
- opt-in with a configurable guard size
- detect only an address inside the guard (a SETUP during a control OUT
  data stage advances from a data buffer that may sit lower)
- EP0 OUT status stage also points DOEPDMA0 past the guard
- the ISR queues only the deferred recovery, UNPLUGGED is sent from it
- stop endpoint/ISO processing once recovery starts
- declare the callback in usbd.h instead of dwc2_esp32.h

Co-authored-by: Tomas Rezucha <tomas.rezucha@espressif.com>
fix(dcd/dwc2): Fix reaction on back2back short SETUP packets

dwc2: re-opening an endpoint with a larger packet is not supported

Drop the TX FIFO grow on re-open and the per-endpoint periodic RX size tracking from 3c16e7fed: an endpoint keeps the FIFO and periodic RX share it was first opened with, and a re-open asserts its packet fits. Isochronous endpoints reserve their largest packet with dcd_edpt_iso_alloc(). Saves the 32-byte size array.

Refs #4454

dwc2: address review of the follow-up sweep

dcd: a TX FIFO grow that does not fit leaves dfifo_top and the endpoint's FIFO as they were; a periodic OUT endpoint re-opened with a larger packet adds the difference to the HS slave periodic RX sum.

hcd: an overcurrent reported with a connect detect in the same port interrupt is not queued as an attach first, and hcd_port_connect_status() reports no device while the port is in overcurrent; the MDATA continuation of a slave interrupt split IN keeps the packet's starting toggle in the channel and continues inside a multi-packet transfer; a failed transfer drops the packet's tentative MDATA bytes.

Review: Greptile and CodeRabbit on #4515

dwc2: keep an IN endpoint's TX FIFO when it is re-opened without close

dwc2 defines TUP_DCD_EDPT_ISO_ALLOC, so usbd_edpt_close() is a no-op and a class that re-opens an endpoint on SET_INTERFACE (video bulk VS) called dfifo_alloc() again: every re-open lowered dfifo_top until the space assert failed and the request stalled. Reuse the endpoint's FIFO, growing it only when it is the last one allocated. A re-opened periodic OUT endpoint likewise no longer adds to the HS Slave periodic RX sum again.

Refs #4454

dwc2: bound the TX FIFO number by GHWCFG4.INEps

With dedicated TX FIFOs the core implements DIEPTXFn only for n = 1..INEps (Databook v4.20a), but the bound came from the per-chip ep_in_count, which only ESP32 sets. nRF54H20 (16 endpoints, 8 IN) let IN endpoints 8..15 program an unimplemented FIFO. Derive the count from GHWCFG4 at FIFO init, keep ep_in_count as a lower override, and skip GD32VF103 and shared-FIFO cores.

Refs #4283

fix(dcd/dwc2): ignore stale USB suspend interrupts

Acknowledge latched suspend interrupts, then check DSTS.SUSPSTS before masking the interrupt or notifying the device stack. This keeps a stale interrupt from reporting a suspend after wakeup.

dwc2: open an IN endpoint beyond the TX FIFOs without one, refuse its transfers (#4448)

Interrupt IN endpoints numbered at or above ep_in_count (e.g. arduino-esp32's CDC notification 0x85 on ESP32-S2/S3) open without a TX FIFO instead of failing SET_CONFIGURATION; transfers on them are refused and their STALL skips the TX FIFO flush. Fixes #4446.

Fixes #4007

dwc2: test rh_init speed first to keep clang -Wunreachable-code quiet

With TUD_OPT_HIGH_SPEED = 0, !TUD_OPT_HIGH_SPEED is a constant true left
operand, so clang flagged the rh_init->speed comparison as never executed.

dwc2: arm EP0 OUT status stage DMA at the setup buffer

In buffer DMA mode the EP0 OUT status stage was armed with DOEPDMA0 =
xfer->buffer, which usbd passes as NULL. A SETUP received while that
status stage is armed (host aborting or retrying a control transfer) was
DMA-written to address 0, and handle_epout_dma() then read the request
from DOEPDMA0 - 8: BusFault at BFAR 0 on STM32U5A5 OTG_HS.

Point DOEPDMA0 at the setup buffer whenever EP0 OUT is armed with zero
length, and skip the DOEPDMA-derived cache invalidate for that case.

Fixes #4327

Merge pull request #3984 from shinoryo1216/fix/dwc2-rxfifo-fallback

dcd/dwc2: size the RX FIFO by the packets that can be pending

dcd_dwc2: reserve one packet per periodic OUT endpoint only at high speed

At full speed a packet takes much longer on the bus than to pop from the
RX FIFO: with room for the 2 largest packets, the USB interrupt still has
~50 us (STM32F407 OTG_FS, 3 x 64-byte interrupt OUT per frame) before a
third periodic packet would be refused, enough when its priority is right.
Keep the per-periodic-endpoint reservation for high-speed Slave mode only,
where popping a packet takes about as long as the bus delivers the next.

dcd_dwc2: size the RX FIFO by the packets that can be pending

The RX FIFO was always sized at 2 x the largest OUT packet, asserted when
the endpoint opened. On small FIFOs that refused valid configurations, for
example a 776-byte FS isochronous OUT on ESP32-S2/S3 (256 words) (#3983).

Size it by what the core can actually receive back to back, in words with
each packet = max packet size / 4 rounded up:

  GRXFSIZ = 13 + 1 + max(L + 1, (P1 + 1) + (P2 + 1), Slave ? S : 0)
            + 2 x EPOUTnum

  L       largest OUT packet of any endpoint, EP0 included: the core admits
          an OUT only while the free space holds that endpoint's max
          packet size
  P1, P2  the 2 largest of {B, B, I1, I2}: B the largest bulk packet
          (counted twice, it can arrive back to back), I1, I2 the 2
          largest periodic (isochronous, interrupt) packets
  S       sum of (packet + 1) over all periodic OUT endpoints. In Slave
          mode the CPU pops the FIFO about as fast as the bus fills it, so
          a further periodic packet in the same (micro)frame would be
          refused: lost (isochronous) or retried one interval later
          (interrupt). Buffer DMA drains fast enough for P1 + P2.
  EPOUTnum  OUT endpoints of the hardware configuration (ep_count), not
          only the active ones, as the core reserves them regardless

The state is kept as these aggregates. As for TX FIFOs, each endpoint is
allocated once per configuration: isochronous endpoints with alternate
settings preallocate their largest packet with dcd_edpt_iso_alloc().

RX only grows when an OUT endpoint opens, so whether a configuration fits
does not depend on the order endpoints open in. A configuration that does
not fit now logs the words it needs, and suggests Buffer DMA where the core
has it.

dwc2: allow forcing device full speed on HS PHY

dcd_init() only programmed DCFG.DSPD for full speed when it picked the
dedicated FS PHY. A core with only an HS PHY (STM32U5A5/H7RS/N6 OTG_HS,
UTMI+) therefore always enumerated at high speed, even when
CFG_TUD_MAX_SPEED or rh_init->speed asked for full speed, serving the
full-speed descriptors on a high-speed link.

Use DSPD = 01 (full speed on the HS PHY) when TUD_OPT_HIGH_SPEED is off
or the port is initialized with TUSB_SPEED_FULL, matching what the host
side already does with HCFG.FSLS_ONLY.

dwc2: serialize slave TX FIFO writes and flushes across cores (#4234)

On dual-core targets the slave-mode ISR TX FIFO write and the TX FIFO flush ran unlocked against the task on the other core, truncating packets (#4229). Take usbd_spin_lock around both.

Add board support for APM32F103 and APM32F107 development boards

This commit adds initial BSP support for Geehy APM32F103 and APM32F107
series development boards in TinyUSB.

- Add board definitions and pin mappings for apm32f103_dev_board and
  apm32f107_dev_board
- Configure USB peripheral clocking and basic board initialization
  (LED, button, UART)
- Update MCU family detection and related build system files to recognize
  the new boards

dcd_dwc2: serialize GINTMSK and DAINTMSK read-modify-write (#4115)

Take usbd_spin_lock around the task and ISR RMWs of GINTMSK/DAINTMSK; on multi-core a stale write could leave RXFLVLM masked or lose SOFM.

Fixes #4105

dcd_dwc2: replace diepempmsk comment block with per-site one-liners

dcd_dwc2: serialize diepempmsk read-modify-write with usbd_spin_lock

diepempmsk gates the TXFE (TxFIFO empty) interrupt of every IN endpoint in a
single 32-bit register, and two places read-modify-write it:

  edpt_schedule_packets()  sets the endpoint's bit
  handle_epin_slave()      clears the endpoint's bit

They touch *different* endpoints' bits of the *same* word, so a write based on a
stale snapshot wipes the other writer's bit.

Observed interleaving (core0 = USB ISR, core1 = task submitting CDC data):

  core0 (ISR)                                core1 (task)
  set ep2: 0x00 -> 0x04
                                             read 0x04, write 0x14
  clear ep2: read 0x04 (stale)
             write 0x00  ------------------> ep4's just-set bit is gone too

The victim is a bulk IN endpoint: its gate is now closed, so the already armed
transfer (DIEPTSIZ.XferSize > 0) never gets its TXFE interrupt, nothing is moved
into the TxFIFO, and the transfer never completes - a bulk endpoint is only
re-armed on completion. Isochronous endpoints re-arm every frame and therefore
self-heal, which is why the failure presents as "audio keeps working, CDC
silently dies".

Latch snapshot: DIEPTSIZ.XferSize > 0, DTXFSTS = 0, the endpoint's diepempmsk
bit cleared.

The set side is already serialized: it only runs for non-EP0 endpoints, and
dcd_edpt_xfer()/dcd_edpt_xfer_fifo() hold usbd_spin_lock() across the whole
scheduling (dcd_edpt_close_all() zeroes the same register under that lock as
well). The clear side runs in the endpoint ISR, which does not hold it, so take
the same lock there - around the epin->tsiz read as well as the update. The ISR
queues the transfer completion before reading tsiz, so the task can re-arm that
endpoint in between, and a clear based on the pre-arm tsiz would wipe the bit of
the transfer that was just armed.

That is deliberately the existing lock and not a dedicated one: OSAL spinlocks
must not be nested. On OPT_OS_NONE each spinlock keeps its own nesting count, so
releasing an inner lock re-enables interrupts while the outer critical section
is still running. Sharing it also keeps a single protection domain for the
register.

Validated on ESP32-S3 with ESP-IDF 6.0 (composite UAC + CDC-ACM + DFU, host
recording audio and streaming CDC at the same time): putting a critical section
around these two statements took the latch rate from 4 events / 6120 s to 0
events / 9600 s (~2.0e8 mask writes). That run serialized them with a separate
OSAL spinlock in espressif/tinyusb 0.19.0~3; this patch gives the same mutual
exclusion through the lock the writers already share.

feat(dcd/dwc2): Add Periodic Transfer Interrupt feature

Enable DCTL.IgnrFrmNum in Buffer DMA so ISOC endpoints can be armed
without even/odd frame matching. This is required to schedule ISOC OUT
on alternating 7/8 ms intervals (Bluetooth HCI 7.5 ms) while keeping
bInterval = 1.
Gated by CFG_TUD_DWC2_PTI_ENABLE (default off, DMA only). When on,
mask IncompISOCIN and report dropped ISOC OUT (PktDrpSts) as a failed
transfer.
